entities.text: ORDER Alagani Sai Pragna vs T.C. Pavan Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard Sri V.Nitesh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Perused the contents of the affidavit filed by the petitioner.

The averments in the affidavit filed by the petitioner phma facie shows that the petitioner is none other than the wife of the respondent/husband, due to the matrimonial disputes between both the parties, the petitioner/ wife is residing separately at Tirupathi at her parents' house along with her female child.

The averments in the affidavit of the petitioner prima facie further shows that the petitioner lodged a complaint against the respondent under Section 498-A, 323, 354A(1)(ii), 354-A{2) of IPC and 3 and 4 of DP Act, and the same is registered as Crime No.103 of 2023 and it is numbered as C.C.No.45 of 2024.
She also filed D.V.C.No.1 of 2025, on the file of III Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Tirupathi and the same are pending for adjudication.

entities.text: III Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Tirupathi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the respondent/husband filed F.C.O.P.No.250 of 2025, before the learned Judge, Family Court-cum-VII Additional District Judge,
Ananthapuram, seeking dissolution of marriage, under Section 13(1) (ia) (ib) of Hindu Marriage Act,
1955 and the same is pending for adjudication.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would further contend that the petitioner/wife has been residing Separately at Tirupathi in her parents' house and the distance between the Tirupathi and Ananthapur is approximately 300 Kms and it is very difficult for the petitioner/wife to attend the divorce case proceedings before the learned Judge, Family Court-cum-VII Additional District Judge,
Ananthapuram, on each and that she is every adjournment without any rhale assistance and constrained to file the present transfer petition.
Perused the record.
Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and for the reasons mentioned in the accompanying affidavit, there shall be an interim stay of all further proceedings including the appearance of the petitioner, i.e., the respondent in F.C.O.P.No.250 of 2025, before the learned Judge, Family Courtrcum-Vll Additional District Judge, Ananthapuram, seeking dissolution of marriage, till 29.01.2026.
